hypothesis: The digest-capture lane's filed adjacent gap (record 20260928-170100, bench fb69eb6): the port's digest relevance-terms window selects the OLDEST four recent texts where the TS anchor takes the NEWEST four - harness_digest.rs recent_message_texts_newest_first collects the chronological user/assistant texts then truncate(4) (the chronological head) then reverse, while TS _buildHarnessDigestQueryTerms (agent-session.ts:9584-9610, the .slice(-4) at 9589) keeps the newest four. The name promised newest-first; the selection kept the head - the name/behavior mismatch is how the divergence survived. The lane's job: reproduce at the tip (a >=5-text window where the two selections differ, the digest terms visibly ranking the wrong rows), inventory every digest_query_terms call site with its TS anchor, implement the TS-parity restore (newest-4), keep the digest-capture placement Oracle A/B green (the ENTER shield), scope the harness-search path honestly, and ship record + PR.
approach: PARITY-FIX, oracle-first red-first. (1) RED AT THE TIP: harness_digest/direction.rs (a new #[cfg(test)] child module at the harness_digest.rs tree position, mirroring compact_session::tests - zero overlap with the digest-capture lane's EOF append, mergeable both ways) ships 3 oracles through the product's own path (wire rows via session_message_to_loop into the live AgentSession context; harness_digest_inputs()): (a) digest_terms_rank_the_newest_four_texts - the >=5-text reproduction with distinct keywords: the newest four carry the exact TS ladder (2.0/1.5/1.0/1.0) and the evicted oldest texts never reach the terms, with the served-path assertion that the selected window IS the newest four; (b) digest_direction_differential_across_window_shapes - the differential across window shapes: base-selection terms (the shipped truncate(4)-oldest shape kept as the A-side mirror, test-only) vs the engine's, where the selections coincide (windows <=4 texts; all-identical >=5-text windows) the renders are byte-identical AND the fingerprints identical (the fingerprint never sees the terms, TS #2400), where they differ (>=5 distinct texts) the renders diverge with the direction-invariant fingerprint and the engine's terms exactly the newest-4 selection's; (c) digest_ranks_the_newest_texts_memory_first - the user/model-visible ranking flip: two keyword-distinct memories on disk, the newest texts' memory must render first. The red gate (crates mode, VM) ran at the test-only head: 3/3 direction oracles red (foxtrot None vs Some(2.0) on the newest text's term; the engine's term map EQUAL to the oldest-4 selection captured verbatim in the panic), 942 other lib tests green. (3) VERIFICATION: green crates gate at the fix head; fold of the tip e4fc1839c at the clean boundary with the post-fold re-diff verified hunk-by-hunk (lane vs folded base = exactly the 2-file delta); full gate on the folded head (merge-bar evidence); STACKED run - the folded lane head + the digest-capture branch (24ef25d3c) merged clean on lane/digest-terms-direction-stack 8dea38418, proving their placement Oracle A/B green under the direction fix (both oracle batteries in one tree; their rig windows are <=4 texts, the coincide class, so the ENTER shield content is direction-invariant).

FROZEN SURFACES: the state fingerprint never sees the query terms (TS _harnessDigestWithFingerprint drops queryTerms before fingerprinting, #2400) so staleness/delivery triggers are direction-invariant (asserted); the rendered digest bytes change exactly where the selections differ (>=5-text windows - the parity restore, TS produces the newest-4 ranking there) and stay byte-identical where they coincide (asserted across the coincide classes). ADJACENT EXTRACTOR NUANCES found and DISCLOSED, NOT changed (filed for the queue, their own lanes): (1) window membership - TS slice(-4) counts every user/assistant MESSAGE regardless of text (an empty-text assistant consumes a window slot and its ladder position, agent-session.ts:9584-9589), the port drops empty-text assistants before windowing so an older text-bearing message can enter the window and the ladder shifts; (2) readAssistantText joins multi-block assistant text with "" (agent-session.ts:1433-1437) where the port joins with " " - only visible for multi-block assistant messages, but it changes the tokenizer input.
